title: Frank Johnson's change of style and Polites resigns in 1956
summary: Frank Traynor replaced Dyer, but Johnson moved toward a mainstream style under Armstrong's influence and Polites and others resigned by the end of 1956.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Well, what about that band? Did it continue on the Frank Johnson band?

It, uh, did continue, um, using, uh, quite a good trombone player, Frank Traynor, uh, on trombone. But, um, by this time, um, Frank Johnson's, uh, uh, idea was, uh, changing. He was, uh, under the bad influence, unfortunately, of, uh, Louis Armstrong. He was one of the first, uh, jazzmen we heard in, uh, in the flesh in Australia. Um, he started to, uh, try and play, um, in a more modern style. Um, not modern jazz, but in a mainstream sort of style. Um, which, uh, didn't suit a lot of us. Um, so that, uh, uh, by the end of 1956, I resigned. Although the band was, uh, getting a lot of work, it was, uh, not playing the same sort of music and, uh, wasn't very satisfactory. Um, so quite a few of us, uh, resigned. He got another band of, uh, rather smart players, uh, good technical players, but they, uh, they didn't have any body, really, in their playing. And, uh, breakups, you know.
